title: Knowledge check: Search Integration

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed for “Search Integration”?
options: A complete substitute for server-side validation
A guarantee that every database write succeeds atomically
A feature that is always enabled without configuration
questions.explanation: The supplied Django curriculum lists “Database-backed search” under lesson 268, “Search Integration”. The lesson connects this item to the practical Django workflow for advanced ecosystem and specialized applications.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports reliable work on “Search Integration”?
options: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
Assume the browser is trusted and skip server-side checks.
Copy a production secret into the source file so every environment matches.
Publish an example before checking framework/version compatibility.
questions.answer_key: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
questions.explanation: Small reproducible examples, server-side validation where relevant, and explicit positive/negative checks help distinguish expected behavior from assumptions. Version, environment, and boundary cases should be documented.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most appropriate when applying “Search Integration” in a real application?
options: Retry every error forever with no backoff or uniqueness check.
Treat a successful HTTP status as proof a remote payment is settled.
Expose all internal error messages and credentials to clients.
Validate external input, set timeouts, handle failures, and make retried work idempotent.
questions.answer_key: Validate external input, set timeouts, handle failures, and make retried work idempotent.
questions.explanation: The lesson is part of Advanced Ecosystem and Specialized Applications. Select the approach that supports correctness, safe handling of failures, and verifiable behavior; see the linked official documentation for version-specific details.

notes: Answer keys and explanations remain in the server-side course repository. The existing CodeLeaf GET handler strips answers until grading; this course does not expose solutions in public lesson content.
